To sample the number of inner vertices $n-1$ (total vertices $n+1$ including endpoints), use the second-moment-based distribution [S1]:

The claim states that to sample the number of inner vertices $n-1$ (for total vertices $n+1$), one should use the second-moment-based distribution [S1]. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes an algorithm for sampling the number of bridge vertices (Section 4 and the summary of contributions). It states that the method stochastically evaluates the sum of multiple bridge estimators ($B_n$) by selecting a single term with probability $P_n$. The evidence specifies that $P_n$ is proportional to the square root of the second moment of the estimator ($P_n ∝ sqrt(E[B_n^2])$) to handle residual variance. This matches the claim's description of using a 'second-moment-based distribution' to sample the number of vertices.
